text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday it had raised prices for oil products, including petrol, by between five and 12 percent due to pressure from global cost increases.

Official media quoted Le van Tan of the Government Pricing Commission as saying the move had been brought into effect on Sunday and was likely to have a knock-on effect on inflation through increased production costs in a number of industries.
He said electricity would cost 12.6 percent more, cement between three and eight percent more and transportation fares would be raised by between three and five percent.
Vietnam is an oil producer but has no refining facility at present, forcing it to export crude and then reimport refined products.

Fuel costs have already increased several times this year. Tan said the inflationary impact of the latest rise was likely to be felt next year, but added that Hanoi still expected 1997 inflation to remain below 10 percent.
Year-on-year inflation stood at 3.8 percent in November.
